X_eliz.note: Came to America in 1860; after her husband's death she ran a hotel in Rollingstone. Her sister Margaret Lehnertz Michels (1839–1931) was born at Heffingen, so Elizabeth probably came from there too. A Find a Grave note names her parents as Michael Lehnertz and Elisabeth Neuhegen. Her death certificate (no. 16846, 12 January 1926, Rollingstone Township) gives her age as 81, birth in Luxembourg, husband Henry Rivers and father's surname Lehnertz. Probable parents Michael Lehnertz and Elisabeth Neuhengen, married at Heffingen 28 Feb 1821 (KB-18, pg=104); their daughter Anna Margaritha, b. 21 Jan 1839 (pg=68), is very probably her sister Margaret Michels. Elizabeth’s own baptism not found 1839–1847. CONFLICT: Washington State death record for her sister Margaret Michels (d. Ellensburg 28 Nov 1931, aged 92, b. 22 Jan 1839 Luxemburg; spouse Martin Michels) gives her maiden name as 'Leonards' and father as 'Peter Leonards', mother blank (Ancestry colls. 60229/1208/6716, index only; FHL film 2022801). X_jacobjohnssr.note: Explicitly named father of Jacob Johns in his son's contemporary 1895 biography. Described as living in Winona County at age ninety-four. No exact birth date inferred. Both he and Maggie brought their son to America when he was three, landing at Baltimore, then living in Missouri and Hazel Green, Wisconsin before settling in Hart Township in 1856. In the 1885 Hart Township census the 84-year-old Jacob is listed with a wife named Rosina, not Maggie; whether he had married again by then or the two names stand for one woman is not known (lead).

X_maggiejahn.note: Named as Maggie (Jahn) Johns, mother of Jacob Johns, in his 1895 biography. Her full given name, dates and birthplace are not established.

X_frederickbutturff.dp: North Middleton Township, Cumberland County, Pennsylvania
X_frederickbutturff.note: Named as Sarah Butturff Hall’s father in the 1884 biography of her husband George W. Hall. Pennsylvania association; no birth or death dates supplied. Samuel is explicitly Sarah’s brother, but the source does not separately state his parents. Named as Sarah's father at her christening at the First Evangelical Lutheran Church, Carlisle, in 1833, when she was eight. Very probably the Frederick Buttorf(f) of North Middleton Township, Cumberland Co., whose two farms north of Middlesex (153 and 84 acres, with brick houses, on the Conodoguinet) and 46 acres of chestnut land in Carroll Twp., Perry Co., were advertised for sale for his heirs on 20 Sept. 1860 by George Buttorf and Philip Kehl (Carlisle Herald, 8 Aug. 1860); administrators’ account March 1862. Shown as “F. Battorff” (two dwellings) on Bridgens’s 1858 county map. Witnessed George Nickey’s will, Frankford Twp., 1839. Identification probable; the estate papers naming heirs are not yet read. 1850 census, North Middleton (image read): Frederick Butorf, 65, farmer, b. Pa., real estate $5000, with Elizabeth 60 and Ann 25. Letters of administration not found in the Cumberland Administrators Book E-F for Mar 1860-May 1861. Parents: lead, Leonard Butdorff of East Pennsborough (will 1818, names sons George, Frederick, John, Leonard and wife Margaret). Leonard Butdorff's 1818 will (image read): executors his son George Butdorff and George Swartz; witnesses Samuel Rees and Jno. Clendenin; no residence for Frederick. Census indexes: Leonard 'Buttery', East Pennsborough, 1810; George Buttorff, East Pennsborough, 1820; George and John Buttorf, Silver Spring, 1830; 'Fredt Buttorp', Frankford Twp., 1830 (11 in household). Frederick's parents still a lead.

X_elizabethbutturff.note: Named as Sarah Butturff Hall’s mother in the 1884 biography of George W. Hall. Her own maiden surname and dates are not supplied. Butturff is her married family name, not an established maiden name. Very probably the Mrs. Elizabeth Buttorff, “wife of Frederick Buttorff, deceased,” who died at Mechanicsburg “on the 25th inst.” [October], aged 77 y. 5 m. 21 d. (American Volunteer, Carlisle, 7 Nov. 1867), so born about early May 1790. Identification probable. 1850 census, North Middleton: Elizabeth Butorf, 60, consistent with b. May 1790.

X_samuelbutturff.note: Explicitly Sarah Hall’s brother and George W. Hall’s furniture-store partner at Wabasha beginning in 1857. Parentage and dates are not separately stated in the source and are left blank.

X_ernestgustavbrose.note: Son of Ernest and Augusta Brose. World War I veteran and Northwestern Railway yardmaster, retired in September 1948. Married Lydia Zambrocki on 1 June 1949. Buried at Saint Mary’s Cemetery, Winona. These details appear in a transcription of the Winona Daily News notice of 2 June 1965, p. 7.

X_louisebrose.note: Daughter of Ernest and Augusta Brose. Married Max E. Schulze on 2 January 1911; their children were Arthur M. Schulze and Ruth Louise Urness. Buried at Woodlawn. The family relationships appear in a transcription of the Winona Daily News notice of 19 April 1962; the precise birth date comes from the memorial index.

X_minniebrose.note: Live memorial explicitly calls her daughter of Ernest/Augusta and wife of William Julius Schellhas. Independently named as sister in Ernest 1965 and Louise 1962 obituary transcriptions. Dates from memorial fields; burial Woodlawn.

X_idabrose.note: Identified as Ida Skow, a deceased sister, in Louise’s 1962 family notice. Parent links and dates are listed in her cemetery memorial; an original vital record is still needed for confirmation.

X_johnhbrose.note: Identified as a deceased brother in Louise’s 1962 family notice. Dates and parent links are listed in his cemetery memorial. Buried at Woodlawn, Section AA, Lot 66.

X_maxschulze.note: Husband of Louise Brose, married 2 January 1911. Her 1962 family notice records that he died in 1956.

X_williamschellhas.note: Named as Minnie Brose’s husband in her cemetery memorial biography. His birth year is given as 1883. The relationship remains probable pending a marriage record.

X_archwilliams.note: Birth and death years are on his grave marker. A transcribed contemporary obituary gives 27 November 1871 in Tennessee and names wife Fannie Racer and brothers Bud, Cleve and John. His placement as a son of Thomas and Rebecca remains probable.

X_williamhenrywilliams.note: The cemetery account gives 1870–1952 and an unmarked burial beside Maud. Arch’s family notice names a brother Bud; the family portrait caption names William. Identification and parentage remain probable.

X_johnarthurwilliams.note: Named John Arthur in the family caption for the back-left man in the five-brother portrait. Arch’s family notice names a surviving brother John Williams of Dallas. Identification and parentage remain probable; dates are unknown.

X_georgewilliams1891.note: Dates are legible on his grave marker. The family account identifies Thomas and Rebecca as his parents and places George at front right in the group photograph. Parentage remains probable. Accounts disagree about his marital status. Texas convict no. 29903: convicted of horse theft in Grayson County on 10 August 1909, received at Huntsville on 17 September 1909, pardoned 15 April 1910 (Texas Convict and Conduct Registers, Ancestry). The register gives his birth as 1892 in Mississippi.

X_fannieracer.note: Original grave photograph confirms 1885–1963. Arch obituary explicitly names his wife as former Fannie Racer of Collinsville and says married 23 years before his death; exact wedding date not derived.

X_maudswett.note: Her marker names Maud, wife of W. H. Williams, born 17 May 1879 and died 18 October 1902. The surname Swett comes from the cemetery family account and remains probable.

X_katherineriversreiland.note: Daughter of Henry and Elizabeth (Lehnertz) Rivers. Married Michael N. Reiland on 20 August 1891. Distinct from Katherine Frisch, wife of Matthew Rivers.

X_michaelnreiland.note: Taught twelve years in Winona public schools before entering the general dry-goods business at Rollingstone in 1892. Had served ten years as village clerk by the 1913 biography and also as school treasurer. Trade-press notices (Telephony, 1908 to 1928) name him an incorporator of the Rollingstone Telephone Company (26 September 1908), its vice-president in 1909 and its secretary by 1920 and 1921; the 1913 county history lists “M. N. Railand” among the incorporators of the First State Bank of Rollingstone (2 January 1905). See story reiland-rollingstone-years. His 1947 obituary gives birth at Granville, Wis., 6 Apr 1861 (tree: 1862); the 1941 golden-wedding report says he had lived at Rollingstone all his life. Conflict left for the owner.

X_peterreiland.note: Arrived in America in 1854 and married Christine Krier at Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, in 1857. Bought 80 acres in Norton Township in 1862 and expanded to 200; retired to Rollingstone in 1900. His exact Luxembourg birthplace is not specified. Lead: Fels (Larochette) baptisms, 11 Jul 1823, Petrus Reuland, son of Joannes Reuland and Catharina Philippi (KB-02, pg=153). The village fits the WikiTree index; the date does not (2 Jun in 1913, 6 Jun in WikiTree). Not linked; b field left as is. 1860 census, Town of Menomonee, Waukesha Co., Wis. (P.O. Menomonee Falls), p. 785, dw. 166, 8 Jun 1860 (image read): Peter Rolland, 40, farmer, $300, b. Luxembourg, with Christiana, 27, b. Luxembourg, no children. Fits the 1857 Menomonee Falls marriage; ages a few years high. Probable. Also at Granville in 1860 (p. 38): Anna Rieland, 30, 'wife', b. Luxembourg, and Nichol 5/12, at the end of the Peter Klehr dwelling - kinship unknown (lead).

X_christinekrier.note: Married Peter Reiland in 1857 at Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin; died in 1898. No parents or death place named in this source. Probably the Christiana, 27, b. Luxembourg, wife of Peter Rolland, Menomonee, Waukesha Co., Wis., 8 Jun 1860 (p. 785, dw. 166, image read).

X_arthurpreiland.note: Teaching school in Winona County when the 1913 biography was published.

X_leonardjreiland.note: Working in the grocery business in Rollingstone in 1913.

X_adelaidereiland.note: Attending St. Mary Domestic Science School at Sparta, Wisconsin, in 1913.

X_lorendareiland.note: Living at home when the 1913 biography was published.

X_winifred_nelton_beeman.note: Her 1966 obituary gives 4 March 1882; a likely 1900 census entry gives March 1883 and later census ages also suggest 1883. The early record names Arthur O. Beeman’s wife Alvina; the identity is probable, and her mother’s name differs across the records.

X_audrey_johnson_king.note: Born to Joel Johnson and Winnie Bozarth; married Riley James King in Paris, Texas, on 29 December 1928.

X_riley_james_king.note: Rancher of Sterling City; married Audrey Johnson in 1928.

X_bonnie_ruth_king_alley.note: Daughter of Audrey Johnson and Riley King; married Marvin Eugene Alley in 1952.

X_marvin_eugene_alley.note: Farm supervisor in Saudi Arabia and later a Texas rancher and land appraiser.

X_robert_eugene_alley.note: Son of Bonnie Ruth King and Marvin Eugene Alley.

X_arthur_oscar_beeman.note: Husband of Winnie Nelton; the 1932 Minnesota death index and memorial list Arthur O. Beeman.

X_arthur_chester_beeman.note: Son of Winnie and Arthur O. Beeman; the dates are from a memorial index.

X_harold_oscar_beeman.note: Son of Winnie and Arthur O. Beeman; the dates are from a memorial index.

X_berniece_beeman_jaszewski.note: Daughter of Winnie and Arthur O. Beeman. The 1950 census records her as Bernice Raboin; her dates come from a memorial index.

X_john_canfield_senior.note: A John Canfield headed the Pennsylvania household containing John A., age two in 1850 and twelve in 1860, with Margaret and the same older children. Those censuses predate the relationship column, so the proposed father-son relationship is probable. His birth is estimated from the recorded ages, not an exact birth record. Very probably the John Canfield of Linesville, Crawford Co., Pa., acknowledged as a paying subscriber of the Anti-Slavery Bugle (Salem, Ohio) in Sept. 1853 and Aug. 1854.

X_anna_thompson_canfield.note: A Wabasha marriage index names John Canfield and Anna Thompson on 3 April 1884. The 1900 Kellogg household records a Norway-born Annie, married to John A. for sixteen years. The birth-register transcription identifies John and Anna as parents of Walter, Homer, Edith and Ruth. Matching the records remains probable; she is distinct from his first wife Anna Hall. John A. Canfield's 1925 obituary gives her death date; the state death index lists Anna Canfield, Wabasha County, 13 Aug. 1913 (1913-MN-014636).

X_walter_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register records Walter, son of John and Anna, father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway; Walter H., fourteen, appears with John A. and Annie in 1900. On that basis he is probably James Garfield Canfield’s half-brother. Walter Henry Canfield, Kellogg rural mail carrier; married Theresa M. Scott at Conception, 18 Sep. 1917 (Wabasha County Herald, 20 Sep. 1917).

X_homer_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register records Homer, son of John and Anna, with father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway; Homer A., twelve, appears in John A. Canfield’s household in 1900. His later life is not established.

X_edith_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register records Edith B., daughter of John and Anna, father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway. The 1900 household has Edith aged ten, indexed with middle initial S.; the conflicting initial is left unresolved.

X_ruth_canfield.note: The transcribed Wabasha birth register names Ruth Jean, daughter of John and Anna, father born Pennsylvania and mother Norway; Ruth J., seven, appears in John A. Canfield’s household in 1900. Her later life is not established.

X_marion_canfield.note: The original 1910 census names Marion, age two, as daughter of James and Helen Canfield; the original 1920 census lists Marian Canfield, eleven, with Nellie Miller and Helen Canfield. Her 1979 family notice identifies her as Marion E. Huntley, née Canfield, and names sister Helen Nelton. It reports her marriage in Winona on 22 July 1926 and her death on the Sunday before 27 November 1979.

X_tom_miller.note: The original 1920 Winona census names Tom Miller, 28, his wife Nellie, 33, and stepdaughters Marian and Helen Canfield. The names and ages support identifying Nellie with the widow of James Garfield Canfield. A marriage record and Tom’s later life have not been established.

X_john_h_heffernan.note: John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household names Nelly, Maudie, Kathy, Loy and Villy. Helen Miller’s obituary identifies siblings Maude Kling, Catherine Ley, Lloyd and William, and her 1939 Social Security application names John H. Heffernan and Mary Shea as her parents. Her 1948 death index instead records father Patrick Heffernan and mother Ellen Shea. His 1910 obituaries name Mrs. James Canfield among his children, which supports him over the Patrick of Helen’s death index. 1895 Minnesota state census, Winona: John Hefferman 35, Ireland; Mary 33; Frank, Nellie, Kate, Roy, Mabel. 1910 obituaries (Wabasha County Herald 27 Jan.; Irish Standard 5 Feb.) give his birth in Limerick, his 1881 marriage to Mary Helen Shea and his children, so he is the John Hefferman of the 1910 death index (1910-MN-014617). Live-stock commission man at Millville; foreman and car inspector on the Green Bay & Western at Winona for sixteen years. Buried in St. Mary's cemetery, Winona.

X_mary_ellen_shea.note: The 1881 marriage certificate calls her Mary Ellen Shea; her 1903 obituary calls her Mary Helen Shea and names husband John Heffernan and their surviving children Helen, Katie, Loy, Maud and Willie. Her 1900 census entry records birth in Minnesota in March 1863; the obituary gives St. Louis in 1864. The 1903 death register gives parents indexed as Jermia Shay and Ellen Holliham. The 1914 death register of a man corresponding to her brother P. W. Shea gives Jeremiah Shea and Ellen Holland; the maternal surname readings differ. Helen’s 1939 application names John H. and Mary Shea as her parents, while Helen’s 1948 death index gives father Patrick Heffernan and mother Ellen Shea. Both generations remain probable with these conflicting details noted. Irish Standard, 21 Mar. 1903: eldest daughter of Jerry and Ellen Shea of Watopa, born in that township in March 1859 (blurred print; the 1875 census age of 16 agrees); died of consumption. This conflicts with the 1900 census (1863) and another family notice (St. Louis, 1864).

X_maude_heffernan.note: Maudie appears in the 1900 household of John and Mary. Helen Miller’s 1948 obituary names her sister Mrs. Michael Kling, and Maude Kling’s 1958 obituary names John Heffernan as her father. Maude’s obituary gives an 1891 birth and a 1909 marriage, while a 1910 census lists a Maude Hefferman as James Canfield’s single sister-in-law; that marital-status discrepancy remains unresolved.

X_catherine_heffernan.note: Kathy is recorded in John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household. Helen’s 1948 obituary names sister Mrs. John Ley, and Maude Kling’s 1958 obituary names sister Catherine Ley. The proposed relationship to these parents is probable.

X_lloyd_heffernan.note: Loy appears in John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household; Helen’s 1948 obituary names a brother Lloyd. In 1920 Lloyd J. Heffernan lived with Mike and Maud Kling next door to Tom and Nellie Miller. The parent link remains probable.

X_william_heffernan.note: Villy is listed in John and Mary Heffernan’s 1900 household, and Helen Miller’s 1948 obituary names her brother William. The connection and identity are probable; his later life has not been established.

X_jermia_shea.note: Mary Heffernan’s 1903 death-register index transcribes her father as Jermia Shay. Her family notice identifies her parents as Mr. and Mrs. J. Shea and her brother as P. W. Shea of Kellogg. Patrick W. Shea’s original 1914 death register names his father Jeremiah Shea. The records support the identification, which remains probable. Irish Standard, 20 Nov. 1909: born County Kerry 1823, married in Ireland, settled first in St. Louis, came to Watopa about 1858; funeral from St. Agnes, Kellogg, Friday 12 Nov., burial St. Felix cemetery, Wabasha. The death index dates the death 13 Nov. 1909 (1909-MN-013447), which conflicts with the funeral date.

X_ellen_holliham.note: Mary Heffernan’s 1903 death-register index transcribes her mother as Ellen Holliham. Patrick W. Shea’s 1914 original death register names his mother Ellen Holland. Mary’s family notice identifies P. W. Shea as her brother; the two different surname readings remain unresolved. Patrick W. Shea's 1914 death register reads Ellen Holland; Holland cousins (Misses Mary and Sarah Holland) came home for his funeral (Wabasha County Herald, 22 Jan. 1914). This supports Holland over the Holliham of Mary's 1903 register (lead). Ages in the state censuses run from 40 (1875) to 68 (1905); she was described as an invalid for many years.

X_frank_heffernan.note: Frank, seventeen, appears as a son in John and Mary Heffernan’s original 1900 census household. Mary’s 1903 notice says her eldest son died eleven weeks before her but does not name him; Frank’s own death notices of January 1903 show that he was that son. Eldest son. Apprentice at the Winona Daily Herald; tried to rescue a drowning boy in June 1898. Died of consumption aged 20 (Irish Standard 10 Jan. 1903; Wabasha County Herald 1 Jan. 1903).

X_patrick_w_shea.note: Mary Heffernan’s 1903 obituary names her brother P. W. Shea of Kellogg. Patrick W. Shea’s 1914 death register records birthplace Missouri and parents Jeremiah Shea and Ellen Holland. His age and birth-date entries differ by about a year, so his birth is approximate. The identification is probable. Obituary (Wabasha County Herald, 15 Jan. 1914) gives birth at St. Louis on 2 Jul. 1862 and names him the only son of Jeremiah Shea; found dead in bed at the Snake Creek farm. State censuses give ages pointing to about 1857, always born in Missouri.

X_florence_minton.note: Listed in the 1920 Oakes census as Florence Minton, 58, Joel Johnson's mother-in-law. Her 1929 Texas death certificate (no. 13314, "Mrs. Sarah F. Menton") gives her birth as 8 Aug 1861 in Texas and her parents as Warren G. Wilkinson (b. Ky.) and Miss Daugherty (b. Tenn.); the informant was her son M. T. Bozarth. She married Frank P. Bozarth in Lee Co. in 1876 or 1877. That she is the 1920 Florence Minton is probable; her parents are proven from the certificate.

X_aletha_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records Aletha, age 12, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_porter_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records Porter, age 9, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_george_f_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records George, age 6, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_willie_johnson.note: The 1910 Oakes census records Willie, age 4, as a child in Joel and Winnie Johnson’s household. The dates shown are estimates from the census, and later life requires further records.

X_frisch_anna_daughter.note: St. Mary’s Oak Ridge cemetery index names Anna as Jacob Frisch’s daughter in the same lot as Jacob and Annette. It does not explicitly name her mother; the link to Annette is probable.

X_frisch_alois.note: St. Mary’s Oak Ridge cemetery index calls Alois a son of Jacob and Annette, age two. The index marks his dates and grave location uncertain, so his exact birth and death are not established.

X_frisch_raymond.note: St. Mary’s Oak Ridge cemetery index identifies Raymond as the son of John and Margarite Frisch and gives his dates. The 1906 family notice describes an unnamed infant surviving Maggie; the dates make Raymond a plausible match.

X_joel_george_w_johnson.note: Probably Joel Anderson Johnson’s father: the 1880 census lists a five-year-old Joel A. as his son, and a 1900 household includes three names matching Joel’s siblings. The 1880 index gives George’s birthplace as Mississippi and age 29; the 1900 index gives Arkansas and age 53. His parentage is unproved. Extracted birth indexes for probable sisters Sallie Mae and Nannie Lou name a George Washington Johnson; the original records have not been examined. Joel A. Johnson's father in the 1880 Lee Co., Tex., census. Buried Sugar Creek Cemetery, Soper (Find a Grave 57684474), sharing a Father/Mother stone with Rebecca. Not the same man as her brother George Washington Fails (1847–1923, Milam Co.). His own parents are unknown; the Kentucky/Lakeport ancestry in the tree is unproved. A duplicate record from an imported family tree, now merged into this one, named Jonathan T. Johnson (13 Oct 1824–07 Apr 1859) as his parent. That parentage is not verified and is not shown in the tree.

X_joel_m_rebecca_johnson.note: Extracted Lee County birth indexes for Sallie Mae and Nannie Lou Johnson name their parents as George Washington Johnson and Marjorie or Margerie Rebecca Fails. The names fit Joel’s sisters, making Fails a probable birth surname for his mother, but those identifications are not certain and the original records have not been examined. Her parents remain unproved. Maiden name Fails from two extracted Lee Co. birth records of her daughters. Find a Grave (57685052) gives earlier marriages to Peter Coleman Watters (1865, Smith Co., Miss.) and William M. Farmer (1869, Williamson Co., Tex.), unverified. Parents Rayford Fail and Polly Anne Wallace: lead only. A duplicate record from an imported family tree, now merged into this one, named Rayford Fail (16 March 1806–26 January 1885) and Polly Anne Wallace (7 Jun 1814–22 Jul 1893) as her parents. That parentage is not verified and is not shown in the tree.

X_andrew_kocak.note: Elizabeth Kocak Lev’s obituary names Andrew as her father and identifies Evelyn Garms as her sister. The 1930 household and birth index support the connection; it remains probable. The original 1930 census lists him as a widowed head, age 35, and Evelyn, Elizabeth and John as his children. His recorded birthplace is Czechoslovakia; this period jurisdiction does not identify a modern village. MOMS indexes his marriage to Mary Stinar on 27 November 1919, Jackson County certificate H-346. His probable parents are András (Andrew) Kocák and Anna Janasko, from the original 1894 Magyar-Izsép baptism read with the U.S. military-service and NUMIDENT indexes. The 1917 draft original records a single farm laborer employed by John Stinar in Minneota Township; the 1940 original places Andrew, 44, with wife Mary and children including Elizabeth, John and Stephen. The 1942 draft records a self-employed Minneota farmer. The draft birth dates conflict: 24 October 1895 in 1917 and 24 September 1895 in 1942; census ages also vary, so no exact birth date is assigned. The probable baptism identification records birth 25 September 1894 and baptism 26 September; the U.S. military index gives 24 October 1895 and the NUMIDENT index 24 October 1896. The military index agrees with the 1917 draft’s 24 October 1895 date; the 1942 draft instead gives 24 September 1895. The original mother’s surname can also be read Jánosko; U.S. indexes spell it Janasko. The parental identification remains probable and no exact birth date is assigned. His 1967 obituary gives his birth as 12 September 1894 in Austria-Hungary, his parents as Andrew and Anna Janasko Kocak, and his First World War service in France; buried with military rites at St. Joseph's, Lakefield (Worthington Daily Globe, 27 and 30 June 1967). Died 26 June 1967 at the Veterans Hospital, Sioux Falls (dates kept in this note because his birth date varies between records).

X_mary_stinar.note: The 1919 official marriage index names Mary Stinar and Andrew Kocak. Her 1930 death index names spouse Andrew, father Jan Stinar and mother Anna Breznay. These details support the identification; her parents are attached as probable while the original death certificate remains restricted and unexamined. The probable matching 1900 census daughter Mary is born September 1892, age 7; the index reads age 8. The death indexes disagree on birth year (1892/1893) and mother’s spelling (Breznay/Brezney); they describe the same event, not independent confirmation. No earlier generations are attached beyond Jan and Anna. The 1910 original explicitly records Mary E., 17, Minnesota-born, as John Stinar Sr.’s daughter in the continuing Minneota household.

X_elizabeth_kocak_lev.note: Her obituary distinguishes birth mother Mary Stinar from stepmother Mary Pavelko and names sister Evelyn Garms. The official MNHS birth index independently matches her date and gives maternal surname Stinar.

X_mary_adeline_pavelko.note: Stephen Joseph’s mother; Elizabeth’s stepmother. Not attached as Evelyn’s birth mother. Deceased by 2008.

X_stephen_joseph_kocak.note: The funeral-home obituary names his parents and deceased sister Evelyn Garms.

X_john_henry_garms.note: His obituary names parents Henry and Evelyn (Kocak). The father’s identity has not yet been reconciled with the disconnected imported Garms household.

X_john_andrew_kocak.note: Official birth and death indexes agree on name, birth date and maternal surname Stinar. Identification with the brother John named in the family obituaries is probable; the index entries do not name Andrew or Mary in full, so the parental attachment remains probable. The original 1930 census lists John, age two, as Andrew’s son with Evelyn and Elizabeth; the age fits the indexed 1927 birth.

X_jan_stinar.note: Mary Kocak’s 1930 death index names her father Jan Stinar. The probable matching 1900 census household records John Stinor, born November 1851, age 48, a farmer; his 1905 age is 53. The census records his birthplace as Hungary S in 1900 and Austria in 1905, period jurisdictions that do not identify a modern village. Earlier parentage is unknown. The 1932 Jan Stiner death index is not attached as an established identification. The 1910 original records John Stinar Sr., age 56, with wife Annie and children George H., Andrew R., Thomas G., Mary E. and Joseph R.; his recorded age conflicts with the 1900 November 1851 birth entry.

X_anna_breznay.note: Mary Kocak’s 1930 death index names her mother Anna Breznay; an alternate index of the same death reads Brezney. The probable matching 1900 household records Annie, born March 1854, age 46, as John’s wife. The 1905 entry gives Anna age 45, conflicting with 1900; her birth date is uncertain. Her birthplace is recorded as Hungary S in 1900 and Austria in 1905; no modern village is established. Earlier parentage is unknown. Andrew Stinar’s 1964 Minnesota death index gives birth 15 April 1888 and mother’s maiden name Brezney, matching the month and year of the Illinois-born son Andrew in the 1900 household; this is corroboration of a probable identification, not independent proof of siblinghood. The 1910 original records Annie, 53, as John Sr.’s wife. George H., 26 and Illinois-born, probably matches the 1930 Hunter father George, 46 and Illinois-born. The 1940 Lakefield Anna, 83 and widowed, with granddaughter Grace, probably belongs to this family through George and Marie; Grace’s parent names are supplied by the 1930 census and NUMIDENT index. This later identification remains probable; no death date or earlier parents are established.

X_andras_kocak_father.note: The original 1894 baptism names András Kocák as father. A probable matching Lastovce marriage on 23 July 1894 records András Kocák, nineteen, Greek Catholic, of Magyar-Izsép, son of János and deceased Hancsin Mária, marrying Anna Jánoskó. The marriage parents are attached within the probable line; identification of the baptized child with Evelyn’s father remains probable with conflicting U.S. birth dates. No exact life dates or later identity established. Magyar-Izsép (Magyarizsép), Zemplén, is today Nižný Žipov, Trebišov District, Košice Region, Slovakia; Lastovce (Lasztóc) is in the same district.

X_anna_janasko.note: The 1894 baptism names Anna, cautiously read Janasko/Jánosko; U.S. indexes use Annie/Anna Janasko. A probable matching Lastovce marriage on 23 July 1894 records Anna Jánoskó, twenty, Roman Catholic, of Magyar-Izsép, daughter of Mihály and Mária Korpás (surname read cautiously). Its connection to the baptism and American family remains probable. No exact life dates or later identity established.

X_janos_kocak_ancestor.note: Named as a parent in the original Lastovce marriage entry 7, 23 July 1894, for András Kocák and Anna Jánoskó of Magyar-Izsép. The connection of this couple to the September baptism and onward to Evelyn’s father remains probable. No exact birth/death dates, later identity or earlier parents established. The father’s given name appears in the parent clause; his displayed surname follows the child’s surname in that entry.

X_maria_hancsin.note: Named as a parent in the original Lastovce marriage entry 7, 23 July 1894, for András Kocák and Anna Jánoskó of Magyar-Izsép. The connection of this couple to the September baptism and onward to Evelyn’s father remains probable. No exact birth/death dates, later identity or earlier parents established. The marriage calls her deceased; no death date is supplied.

X_mihaly_janosko.note: Named as a parent in the original Lastovce marriage entry 7, 23 July 1894, for András Kocák and Anna Jánoskó of Magyar-Izsép. The connection of this couple to the September baptism and onward to Evelyn’s father remains probable. No exact birth/death dates, later identity or earlier parents established. The father’s given name appears in the parent clause; his displayed surname follows the child’s surname in that entry.

X_maria_korpas.note: Named as a parent in the original Lastovce marriage entry 7, 23 July 1894, for András Kocák and Anna Jánoskó of Magyar-Izsép. The connection of this couple to the September baptism and onward to Evelyn’s father remains probable. No exact birth/death dates, later identity or earlier parents established. Her surname is read cautiously as Korpás in the original handwriting.

X_nicolasfrisch.note: Father of Jacob Frisch. Named, with his wife Maria Simon, "conjugum in Beaufort", in Jacob’s 1837 baptism (Beaufort no. 56) and in his 1862 marriage.

X_mariasimon.note: Mother of Jacob Frisch; of Beaufort. Named in his 1837 baptism and 1862 marriage. A Jacob Simon of Beaufort was the child’s godfather.

X_nicolasspeltz.note: Farmer. Father of Anna Spelz (1836 Fischbach baptism); "defunctus" at her 1862 marriage, the family then in Dickweiler, parish of Rosport. Find a Grave (31369634, unsourced) gives b. 5 Jul 1796 Greiveldange, d. 12 Oct 1859 Dickweiler: lead. Married Catharina Michels at Contern 30 Dec 1822 (‘penultima die anni’), son of the late Nicolas Speltz and Catharina Osch (reading uncertain), formerly of Greiveldange (Contern KB-04, pg=79). Greiveldange’s own early registers are not on Matricula, so the 5 Jul 1796 birth is still a lead.

X_katharinamichels.note: Mother of Anna Spelz (1836 baptism; 1862 marriage). Gravestone at St. Mary’s, Oak Ridge: born Contern 2 Feb 1799, died 9 Jan 1884. Cemetery index puts her in the Frisch lot 49, grave 4, but gives 2 Dec 1799 and maiden name "Wagoner". Baptized Contern 16 Mar 1799, daughter of Nicolas Michels, blacksmith, and Anna Maria Seiwert (Contern KB-02, pg=62); married Nicolas Speltz at Contern 30 Dec 1822, the same parents named (KB-04, pg=79). The b field (2 Feb 1799, gravestone) is left as is.

X_johannadehm.note: Blacksmith (ferrifaber) of Junglinster. Father of Maria Margaretha, baptized 16 Oct 1807; present at her 1832 marriage at Heffingen, where he signed "J. Adehm". Married Margaretha Michaeli at Junglinster, Nov. 1804 (dated 29 Brumaire XIII / 20 Nov 1804), son of Friedrich Adam, blacksmith, and Catharina Peus (reading uncertain) (Junglinster KB-01, pg=65). Proven.

X_margarethamichels.note: Wife of Johann Adam/Adehm of Junglinster; mother of Margaretha Adehm (1807 baptism, "Michaels", reading probable; 1832 marriage, "Michels"). No relationship to Katharina Michels Speltz is known. Written Michaeli at her 1804 Junglinster marriage: daughter of the late Johann Michaeli, blacksmith, and Maria Cass (reading uncertain). Proven.

X_jnrivers.note: Tavern keeper (popinator) at Heffingen; father of Michel Rivers, named in Michel’s 1832 marriage, at which he was present. Baptized Heffingen 18 Oct 1771, son of Nicolaus Rivers and Elisabeth (KB-18, pg=7); ‘hansnekel, 18 [Oct] 71’ in the Rivers house of the 1798 parish list; married Anna Molitor at Heffingen 17 Jan 1799 (pg=99). Parents probable.

X_annamolitor.note: Wife of Johann Nicolas Rivers of Heffingen; mother of Michel Rivers (1832 marriage). ‘anna molitor, 13 jul 73’ in the Bocks house, 1798 list; baptized 13 Jul 1773 as Anna, daughter of Johann Heinrich Müller and Elisabeth Bock (Backs); called ‘Anna Molitor sive Bocs’ in 1804, when her brother Michael Molitor was godfather. Parents probable (strong).

X_warren_g_wilkinson.note: Named as father ("Waren G. Wilkingson", b. Ky.) on the 1929 Texas death certificate of his daughter Sarah Florence Menton (no. 13314). A Warren Gall Wilkinson, brother of San Jacinto veteran James Gore Wilkinson (b. Hardin Co., Ky., 1805), settled with his family in what became Washington Co., Republic of Texas; that he is the same man is a lead. A W. G. Wilkinson was doorkeeper of the Senate of the Republic of Texas, April 1838; a Warren G. Wilkinson Survey (A-670) lies on the San Gabriel in Williamson Co. Link to Florence’s father still a lead.

X_daugherty_wilkinson.note: Mother of Sarah Florence (Wilkinson) Bozarth Menton. The 1929 Texas death certificate gives only "Miss Daugherty", born in Tennessee; her first name is unknown.

X_anton_klemencic.b: 12 Jun 1887 (also given as 2 Jul 1887 and 6 or 9 Jun 1886)

ph.c: Anton Klenskiy's marker, Calvary Cemetery, Omaha

X_anton_klemencic.note: Diane's birth father (probable). Also recorded as Anton Klemencic (1903 passenger list), Tom Klensky (Omaha, 1908–1916), Tom Klenskiy (1917 draft card), Thomas Klensky (1929 marriage, 1932 Omaha directory, 1940 census), Thomas Klinsky (1940 census index), Anton Klenskiy (1942 draft card, 1963 gravestone and Social Security), Anton Klensky (1963 death notice); his brother used Klements. Croatian form: Antun Klemenčić. His parents were most likely Josip Klemenčić (1856–1940) and Dorothea Tomašić (1863–1945) of Ribnik, who married at Lipnik in 1881: Rudolph's 1911 marriage record names a Joseph and a Dorothea, and an independent FamilySearch family tree lists a Tom Klements, born at Ribnik and died in Omaha, among their children. His marriage to Hazel Stevens was on 3 August 1929.

X_george_w_canfield.note: Son of John A. Canfield and Anne Hall (John's 1925 obituary names him as one of their three children); age 9 at Kellogg in 1885. Living at Spooner, Wis., in 1925.

X_wilson_canfield.note: Son of John A. Canfield and Anne Hall (1925 obituary). Wilson 6 in 1885, John W. 16 in 1895. Roseland, Manitoba, in 1912; Carrington, N.D., in 1925.

X_catherine_shea_sullivan.note: Irish Standard, 16 Mar. 1907, names her parents Mr. and Mrs. Jerry Shea of Watopa. Wife of Daniel Sullivan of Highland, a locomotive fireman on the Great Western; lived at Osage, Iowa, then Rochester. Buried St. Felix cemetery, Wabasha.

X_nellie_shea.note: Ellon 10 in 1875, Ellie 30 in 1895, Nellie 38 in 1905 in the Watopa household; named as surviving daughter in her father's 1909 notice and her brother's 1914 obituary ('Miss Nellie Shea, who lives at home'). A 1941 Wabasha County death index entry for Ellen Shea may be hers (lead).

X_marion_tyson.note: Son 'Marion', 17, in Albert and Elizabeth Tyson's household at Oakes in the 1940 census; PFC, U.S. Army, World War II (military marker). Buried Restland Cemetery, Boswell; wife Ruby Mae McKee (1924–2005).

X_penny_johnson_cole.note: Buried Mount Olivet Cemetery, Hugo. Named as Joel A. Johnson's sibling in his 1961 obituary; Find a Grave links to George W. and Rebecca Johnson (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/164499410/elizabeth-cole).

X_nannie_johnson_harrison.note: Buried Soper Cemetery. Named as Joel A. Johnson's sibling in his 1961 obituary; Find a Grave links to George W. and Rebecca Johnson (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/90948220/nannie-harrison).

X_carl_albert_johnson.note: Buried West Side District Cemetery, Taft, Kern Co., California; in his parents' 1900 Choctaw Nation household. Named as Joel A. Johnson's sibling in his 1961 obituary; Find a Grave links to George W. and Rebecca Johnson (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/151948792/carl_albert-johnson).

X_sallie_johnson_smith.note: Wife of Sim Smith (1889–1943); buried Benvanue Cemetery, Byers, Clay Co., Texas. Birth index names her mother Marjorie Rebecca Fails. Named as Joel A. Johnson's sibling in his 1961 obituary; Find a Grave links to George W. and Rebecca Johnson (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/10576629/sallie-smith).

X_william_arthur_johnson.note: Buried Palisade Cemetery, Mesa Co., Colorado; wife Esther Gladys Homan (1892–1976). 'Arthur' in his parents' 1900 household. Named as Joel A. Johnson's sibling in his 1961 obituary; Find a Grave links to George W. and Rebecca Johnson (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/47958989/william_arthur-johnson).

xr1-001.note: Eldest of the children in Jacques and Anna Frisch’s household. The 1875 state census gives his age as 14 and his birthplace as Luxembourg, the only child so recorded; the 1885 census gives 22. He is not with the family in 1895 or 1905. The census recorded no relationships, so the parentage is read from the household (probable). Marriage, death and later life are not established; two Winona County death-index entries for a Nicholas Frisch were not attached because other Frisch families lived in the county.

xr1-002.note: Recorded as Mathias, 12, in 1875; Mathew, 20, in 1885; Matt, 27, in 1895; and Matt, 40, in 1905, when he headed his own household in Mount Vernon Township, followed in the list by an Annie (36, born in Wisconsin of German parents) and three children aged 7, 5 and 1, presumably his wife and children. Parentage is read from the shared household (probable). His wife was Annie Haines, Maggie Haines Frisch’s sister, named as Mrs. Matt Frisch of Oak Ridge in their mother’s 1916 obituary. Date conflict: the state death index gives 15 December 1938 (certificate 1938-MN-016862), while the St. Mary’s Oak Ridge burial list gives 18 December 1938 and a birth date of 11 April 1865. The tree keeps the index date; a newspaper notice or the certificate itself would settle it.

xr1-003.note: Maggie, 10, in 1875 and 18 in 1885; she is not in the household in 1895. She is a different person from her sister-in-law Maggie (Haines) Frisch, who died on 1 October 1906. Parentage is read from the shared household (probable); her later life is not established.

xr1-004.note: Indexed as Elisa, 4, in 1875 and Elisa, 14, in 1885, and as Lizzie, 20, in 1895 (the three ages point to birth years between about 1871 and 1875). Parentage is read from the shared household (probable); she is not in the family’s 1905 households, and her later life is not established.

xr1-005.note: The elder of two sons named John in the household: John Peter, 6, in 1875; John S., 15, in 1885; John P., 24, in 1895; and John P., 34, in 1905, when he is followed in the list by an Emma (35) and three children aged 5, 3 and 1, presumably his wife and children. He is not the younger John (about 1873), the schoolteacher who married Maggie Haines, though family records may have merged the two; the family tree’s John P. Frisch (born 25 July 1873) matches the younger brother by age. Parentage is read from the household (probable).

xr1-006.note: Katherine, 10, in 1885; Katlerin (Katherine), 18, in 1895; and Katie, 28, in 1905, still unmarried in her father’s household after her mother’s death in 1902. Parentage is read from the shared household (probable). She is probably the Katherine Frisch who married Matthew Rivers on 19 November 1907: his 1913 county-history biography names his bride as Kathryn “Trisch,” daughter of Jacques “Trisch,” which reads as Frisch, and story rivers-heffingen quotes a 1934 notice listing Mrs. Mathew Rivers among John Frisch’s sisters. The marriage is linked as probable, not proven; no marriage record has been seen.

xr1-007.note: The youngest child in the household: Virgina, 3, in 1885; Virginia, 14, in 1895; and Virginia, 22, in 1905, still in her father’s household. Parentage is read from the shared household (probable). The St. Mary’s Oak Ridge burial list has her as Virginia Frisch Kronebusch, born 18 August 1881 and dead on 4 May 1950, wife of J. B. Kronebusch (28 January 1881 to 3 June 1959), in lot 65; the list is compiled and no death certificate has been seen. Her birth date replaces the earlier “about 1882”.

xr1-008.note: Eldest of John and Maggie Frisch’s three children: Gertrude, 2, appears with John (31) and Maggie (29) in the 1905 state census, and story frisch-1906 counts her among the three young children left in October 1906. Viola’s 1975 obituary, as quoted in story rivers-rollingstone, names a sister, Gertrude Koetter, who is the same woman (probable; no marriage record seen). The St. Mary’s Oak Ridge burial list gives Gertrude Frisch Koetter, born 7 June 1903 and dead on 4 May 1984, with husband Joseph Koetter (19 May 1905 to 19 June 1981), in lot 44.

xr1-009.note: Listed with Michael (70) and Margaretha (66) Rivers in Norton Township in the 1875 state census, aged 32 and born in Luxembourg, and probably the Frank of the 1865 Rivers household. The census recorded no relationships, so the parentage is read from the household (probable). His later life is not established.

xr1-010.note: Listed with Michael and Margaretha Rivers in 1875, aged 30 and born in Luxembourg. A George Rivers of about the right age (50 in 1895, 61 in 1905) is listed with Elizabeth Rivers and her sons Henry and Edward at Rollingstone; whether he is this George, and whether he was Elizabeth’s second husband or her brother-in-law and partner, is not established (lead).

xr1-011.note: Henry, 18, and Edward, 13, are listed with Lizzie Rivers (47) at Rollingstone in 1895, and Henry, 28, and Edward, 23, with Elizabeth (56) in 1905; Edward is Edward Rivers Sr. (born 1881). Parentage is read from the household (probable). The Winona Daily Herald reports a Henry Rivers of Avoca visiting Rollingstone “folks” in 1896, a Henry Rivers arrested in 1899 as the Avoca agent of the Peavey Elevator company, and a Henry Rivers opening a machinery store at Rollingstone in 1900; whether these are all this Henry is probable but not stated in any record. Jr. is added here to tell him from his father.

xr1-012.note: Indexed as Rosina, 6 months, in the 1885 state census; Rose, 10, in 1895; and Rosella, 20, in 1905, in Jacob and Theresa Johns’s household at Hart Township. Her sister Johanna’s 1967 notice (quoted in story johns-hart-township) names a sister, Mrs. Rose Tiernan of Albertville. The death index entry for Rosella E. Tiernan gives birth on 9 November 1884 in Minnesota, mother’s maiden name Kriezer, and death in Wright County on 28 January 1970. Her husband’s name is not established.

xr1-013.note: Named as a daughter of John and Margaret (Greer) Canfield, “one of ten children,” in the sketch of her second husband, Martin H. Tobias, in the 1920 History of Wabasha County; she taught school in the county, married George Calvin and then, in May 1876, Martin H. Tobias, and died in 1895. A Francis Canfield is listed in John Canfield’s Highland household in the 1865 state census. The 1920 sketch of Joseph C. Schierts misprints the family name as Calvin.

xr1-014.note: Frances Canfield’s first husband, “of Meadville, Penn.” and a native of Pennsylvania, according to the 1920 History of Wabasha County. They had one daughter, Sarah Margaret. He had died before Frances married Martin H. Tobias in May 1876. No dates or places are given.

xr1-015.note: Son of Simon and Elizabeth (Handshue) Tobias; teacher in Pennsylvania and Ohio, came to Minnesota in 1871, clerked at a Kellogg hardware store from 1874, farmed in Cook’s Valley until 1881 and then lived retired in Kellogg, serving as recorder and as justice of the peace for Greenfield township (1920 History of Wabasha County, p. 485). The death index entry for Martin Henry Tobias, Wabasha County, 20 January 1922, is identified with him by name, county and date (probable). He and Frances had six children, five living in 1920, who are named in the story but not added to the tree.

xr1-016.note: Called Sarah M. (Calvin) Odell in the sketch of her husband Joseph C. Schierts and Margaret in the sketch of her stepfather, Martin H. Tobias (1920 History of Wabasha County, pp. 484-486). Widow of Bert Odell, by whom she had two daughters, Vera M. and Bessie; married Joseph C. Schierts on 11 October 1904. The death index entry for Sarah Margaret Schierts, Wabasha County, 9 January 1928, gives both names and is identified with her by name and county (probable).

xr1-017.note: Son of Joseph and Elizabeth (Rohler) Schierts. Lumber-yard manager at Kellogg from 1904 and furniture dealer there from 1913, a bank director and township assessor (1920 History of Wabasha County, pp. 484-485). The Minnesota death index gives the same birth date and his mother’s maiden name, Rohler, with death in Wabasha County on 27 February 1965.

xr1-018.note: Named in George W. Hall’s biography in the 1884 History of Wabasha County (pp. 1283-1284) as the eldest of the sons, living at Greenfield. No dates are given there, and he has not been found in the censuses.

xr1-019.note: Named in the 1884 History of Wabasha County as living at Prairie View, Kansas. “Parker Hall,” 18, born in Iowa, is listed with Sarah Hall (50, born in Pennsylvania) at Greenfield in the 1875 state census, which fits a son born in Iowa during the family’s Muscatine years. A Parker Hall also appears on a 1866 Wabasha school roll of honor (poor OCR; lead).

xr1-020.note: Named as George W. in the 1884 History of Wabasha County, living at Prairie View, Kansas, with his brother William Parker. “Jr.” is added here only to tell him from his father. No dates are given, and he has not been found in the censuses.

xr1-021.note: Listed as James H., 45, born in New York in the 1885 Winona state census, and as Jae H., 57, in 1895 and James, 66, in 1905, in the same household as Arthur Beeman. The 1905 index gives his father’s birthplace as Ireland and his mother’s as New York. No death record was found in the Winona County index.

xr1-022.note: Indexed as Luzinda, 38, in 1885; Lucinda E., 48, in 1895; and Lucinda, 58, in 1905, with both parents born in New York. The maiden name Thurber comes from the death index entry for her son James George Beeman and is probable, not proven. No death record was found in the Winona County index.

xr1-023.note: James G., 14, born in Wisconsin, in the 1885 household of James H. and Luzinda Beeman, and Jae G., 24, in 1895. The death index entry for James George Beeman (born 19 February 1870, out of state, mother’s maiden name Thurber; died Winona County, 20 April 1955) matches by name, age and the Winona household (probable). A Charles H. Beeman, born in Minnesota on 22 December 1872 and dead in Olmsted County on 24 August 1959, may be the middle brother, Charles H., 11 in 1885 (lead only).

xr2-001.note: Named as Mrs. J. M. Hulsey of Van Alstyne among the four surviving sisters in the 1938 funeral notice for her brother Arch. Her dates, her husband and her place as a daughter of Thomas Henry and Rebecca Williams come from a family-sourced typescript (Pearson, A History of the Fee Family, pp. 1271A-1271B), which gives the dates in two places and agrees with itself. No record has been seen.

xr2-002.note: Husband of Callie Williams Hulsey. The 1938 funeral notice for Arch Williams names him only through her, as J. M. Hulsey of Van Alstyne. His dates come from the Pearson typescript; no record has been seen.

xr2-003.note: Mrs. Mollie Crocker of Brownfield in the 1938 funeral notice for her brother Arch; Molly in the Pearson typescript, which gives two possible birth years and her marriage to Ell Crocker on 10 Jul 1898. A 1909 family photograph on this site is captioned with her holding a baby. No death date has been found.

xr2-004.note: Named only in the Pearson typescript, as the husband of Molly Williams (married 10 Jul 1898). Ell may be short for a longer name. The typescript gives their first child, James Otis, a ginner at Brownfield, a birth date of 6 Apr 1899.

xr2-005.note: Mrs. Emma Rockford of Sherman in the 1938 funeral notice for her brother Arch. The Pearson typescript gives her birth as May 1882 and writes her name "Emma (Rockford)", with no husband, children or death date.

xr2-006.note: Mrs. Lillie Fields of Hamlin in the 1938 funeral notice for her brother Arch. The Pearson typescript gives her dates, her marriage to Henry I. Fields and a household in Jones County, Texas, where Hamlin lies. No record has been seen.

xr2-007.note: Husband of Lillie Williams Fields in the Pearson typescript, which gives his death as 13 Jul 1945 in two places and as 1961 in a third.

xr2-008.note: Listed with the same dates, 1928–1964, after Cleave and Willie P. Williams on the Van Alstyne Cemetery page, and named first among Willie's children in the Pearson typescript. Entered as their son; no record seen names his parents.

xr2-009.note: Named in a typescript family history (Pearson, A History of the Fee Family, pp. 1269-1270) as the father of Dorcus McAfee Williams; birth and death years as typed, with the scan of the death year rough. A carpenter, according to the typescript. A Moses McAfee did marry Sarah Chamberlin in Davidson Co., Tenn., on 23 Nov 1798 (record printed in the DAR Magazine, Feb. 1925); the typescript adds a second marriage, to Sally Chamberlain on 31 Dec 1800, which has not been seen. That he is Dorcus's father is a lead only. Pearson's typescript says land was sold as Moses's share of the estate of a Thomas McAfee (Lincoln Co., Tenn.); Thomas is a possible father (lead). Not linked. Ancestry's Tennessee Wills and Probate index (searched 5 Nov 2026) has 104 McAfee entries for Lincoln County but no estate file for a Thomas McAfee (only a later Thomas W. as a non-primary name). The Thomas McAfee estate share is still known only from the typescript.

xr2-010.note: The bride in the Davidson Co., Tenn., marriage of Moses McAfee on 23 Nov 1798 as printed in the DAR Magazine, Feb. 1925 (the digitized year reads 1708, a scanning slip). The typescript spells the surname Chamberlain or Chamberland and says one or both of Moses's wives came from Chamberlain Creek, Georgia. Whether she was the mother of Dorcus is not known, because the typescript gives Moses two wives.

xr2-011.note: Listed first among Moses McAfee's children in the typescript (born Tennessee, 1803; said to have married Harriett (Barnes) Childers). A William McAfee, 47, born in Tennessee, lived two dwellings from Thomas and Dorcas Williams in the 1850 McNairy Co. census, as the Dwelling 1800 story records. That he is Dorcus's brother is a lead.

xr2-012.note: Entered as "John Waters, son, 13" in the household of Geo W. and M. Rebecca Johnson in the 1880 Lee Co., Texas, census, born in Texas of Mississippi-born parents. The Sugar Creek story, citing a Find a Grave memorial, gives his birth as 10 Jul 1866 in Milam Co. and his father as Peter Coleman Watters; the 1880 age fits that date and not the 1861 on his marker. His death is dated 1926 on the marker and 1927 on the memorial.

xr2-013.note: Listed as a daughter, aged 6, in the 1880 Lee Co., Texas, household of Geo W. and M. Rebecca Johnson. Nothing else is known of her.

xr2-014.note: Listed as "Margarett P", a daughter aged 1, in the 1880 Lee Co., Texas, household of Geo W. and M. Rebecca Johnson. Nothing else is known of her.

xr2-015.note: Entered as Geo Fails, 32, farmer, born in Mississippi, with parents born in North Carolina and Alabama, four dwellings from the Johnsons in the 1880 Lee Co., Texas, census (the transcriber read his middle initial as M). The Raford Failes story names George Washington Fail as the eldest son of Rayford Fail and Polly Anne Wallace, born in Jasper Co., Mississippi, in 1847 and married to Margaret Ann Johnson in 1870; that parentage rests on WikiTree and is not confirmed by a record seen here, though his parents' birthplaces fit.

xd5-001.note: Wife of Matt Frisch. Her death index entry gives her mother’s maiden name as Bill, as Maggie Haines Frisch’s 1906 entry does; the Oak Ridge cemetery list names her Annie Haines Frisch, buried beside Mathias. Named as Mrs. Matt Frisch of Oak Ridge among the surviving daughters in Margaret Haines's 1916 obituary; her own records give her mother's maiden name as Bill.

xd5-002.note: Gilbert, 7, in Matt and Annie Frisch’s 1905 household. His death index entry gives his mother’s maiden name as Haines. Buried at St. Mary’s, Oak Ridge.

xd5-003.note: Birth indexed as Cleo Frisch, mother Haines; indexed as Kelan, 1, in the 1905 household. The death index and the cemetery list differ by three days on his death.

xd5-004.note: Birth and death index entries both give his mother’s maiden name as Haines. Buried in his parents’ lot at Oak Ridge.

xd5-005.note: Married John P. Frisch on 19 October 1897 (county marriage index). Emma, 35, follows John P. in the 1905 census, and the Oak Ridge cemetery list names her Emma Kramer Frisch, wife of John. Her parents are not identified.

xd5-006.note: Birth indexed as Waldemar Frisch, mother Kramer; Waldermar, 3, in the 1905 household. The Oak Ridge cemetery list calls him Reverend and son of John and Emma; the death index entry for Edward Waldemar Frisch has the same death date.

xd5-007.note: Daughter of Jos. Burbach, according to the 1894 wedding notice. Married Nick Frisch at Oak Ridge in September 1894. The cemetery list spells her Burback; the county marriage index reads Blirbach.

xd5-008.note: Anna, 16, in George and Eda Nelton’s 1895 household; married Joseph Knopp on 7 January 1899 (county index). Her death index entry gives her mother’s maiden name as Zenk, and Winnie Beeman’s 1966 obituary names a sister Anna Knopp.

xd5-009.note: Joseph Knopp, 39, born in Wisconsin, in Charles Knopp’s Winona household in 1895; 44 in 1905, heading his own household with Anna B. and two children. The two ages do not agree. Michael Knopp’s 1895 biography names a son Joseph who farmed in partnership with his brother Charles, which matches the 1895 household and makes Michael and Gertrude (Doetsch) Knopp his probable parents. The book’s own order of the ten children puts Joseph fifth; his census ages of 39 and 44 still disagree. Death date from his widow's obituary (Winona Daily News, 4 Mar 1974, p. 2), which also gives the marriage as 7 Jan 1898 (index: 1899). The Knopp stone at Woodlawn, Winona (Find a Grave memorial 98313542, grave photo) reads Joseph 1855– and Anna 1879–1974, with a partly hidden marriage line ending ‘99’ (1899 likely), and a small veterans' cross beside it.

xd5-010.note: Birth index gives her mother’s maiden name as Nelton; Helen L., 4, in the 1905 household. Her later life is not established.

xd5-011.note: Joseph H., 1, in the 1905 household; his death index entry gives his mother’s maiden name as Nelton.

xd5-012.note: His death index entry gives his mother’s maiden name as Nelton.

xd6-001.note: Listed as Martha, 16, in the 1850 McNairy Co., Tenn., household of Thomas and Dorcas Williams (as reported in the story "Dwelling 1800, McNairy County") and as "Marth?", 26, unable to read or write, in their 1860 household at Stantonville. Neither census states relationships; she is entered as their daughter because the same parents and the same six children appear together ten years apart. Nothing later is known of her.

xd6-002.note: Sarah, 13, in the 1850 McNairy Co., Tenn., household of Thomas and Dorcas Williams and Sarah, 22, unable to read or write, in their 1860 household at Stantonville. Entered as a daughter because the same family group appears in both censuses; neither states relationships.

xd6-003.note: Catharine, 12, in 1850 and Catherine, 19, in 1860 in the McNairy Co., Tenn., household of Thomas and Dorcas Williams. The two ages imply birth years three years apart. Entered as a daughter on the strength of the two households; neither census states relationships.

xd6-004.note: John, 9, in 1850 and John, 17, a farm laborer who had attended school that year, in 1860, in the McNairy Co., Tenn., household of Thomas and Dorcas Williams. A family typescript (Pearson, A History of the Fee Family) says Thomas Henry Williams's older brother John married a Britton; that has not been checked. Entered as a son on the strength of the two households.

xd6-005.note: Joseph, 6, in 1850 and Joseph, 13, in 1860 in the McNairy Co., Tenn., household of Thomas and Dorcas Williams; the 1860 age implies a birth about three years later than the 1850 age. Entered as a son on the strength of the two households; neither census states relationships.

ph.c: Ben and Mary Ann Bell at home near Rosemond, Texas, early 1920s

X_ben_bell.note: Married Mary Ann Snow in Wayne County, Kentucky, in February 1870 and moved to Collin County, Texas, between 1885 and 1889. His Texas death record gives birth on 15 January 1848 in Wayne County and parents Jerry Mitchel Bell and Nancy Ellen Davis. The 1880 census at Mullentown, Wayne County, shows him at 33 with Polly A. and four children, one of them Charles H., 6. His 1870 marriage record gives his father’s birthplace as Wayne Co. and his mother’s as “CCK” (very probably Clinton Co., Ky.).

ph.c: Ben and Mary Ann Bell at home near Rosemond, Texas, early 1920s

X_polly_snow_bell.note: Married Benjamin Bell in Wayne County, Kentucky, in February 1870. The 1880 census gives her as Polly A., 28, born in Kentucky; her memorial gives 1851 and a 1936 death, and cites a Texas death certificate naming her father as A. J. Snow. Father very probably Andrew Jackson Snow (1823-1911) of Wayne Co.; she was not in his 1860 household (A. J. 36, Arrilla 24, Louisa Jane 12, Martha 8/12), so the link rests on the death-record name, age and county. Her 1936 Texas death certificate gives birth 16 June 1852 at Monticello, Ky., and father A. J. Snow; a mother’s maiden name was begun as “Mary Ann Snow” (her own name) and struck through, and the informant did not know it.

X_jeremiah_bell.note: Named as Jerry Mitchel Bell, father of Ben Bell, on Ben's 1926 Texas death record.
